'''Curry mee'''{{efn|{{lang|ms|mi kari}}; {{zh|s=咖喱面|t=咖喱麵|p=Gālímiàn|j=Gaa3 Lei1 Min6|poj=Ka-lí-mī}}}} is a spicy noodle soup associated particularly with [[Malaysian Chinese cuisine]]. It is commonly prepared with yellow noodles or rice vermicelli in a spiced coconut-milk broth and may contain ingredients such as tofu puffs, cockles, cuttlefish, prawns, chicken and pork products.<ref name=Rasa>{{cite web | url=https://rasamalaysia.com/curry-noodle-soup/ | title=Curry Noodle Soup | website=Rasa Malaysia | access-date=July 12, 2026}}</ref><ref name=Malay1/>

The term overlaps with ''[[curry laksa]]'' in parts of Malaysia, and curry mee is also known as curry laksa in some Malaysian usage. Coconut-based laksa dishes are likewise found in Singapore, although their names, ingredients and preparation vary by region.<ref>{{cite web |title=Malaysian Food: 52 Top Picks You Shouldn't Miss |url=https://www.malaysia.travel/explore/malaysian-food-52-top-picks-you-shouldn-t-miss |website=Malaysia Truly Asia |publisher=Tourism Malaysia |access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Tan |first=Joanna Hwang Soo |title=Laksa |url=https://www.nlb.gov.sg/main/article-detail?cmsuuid=6d5b6967-a680-4449-b3cc-91d03ab44dfd |website=Singapore Infopedia |publisher=National Library Board Singapore |access-date=12 July 2026}}</ref>
